# ALGHREST

Multi-market trading research and decision support, with an advisory-only
Earn2Trade/TCP25 profile. Deterministic data, account, risk and evaluation-policy
checks govern the advice path. AI proposals cannot override those checks.

The project is under development. Strategy edge, complete rule-exact TCP25
simulation, pass/fail Monte Carlo and real-account readiness remain unproven.
Existing agent/execution code is retained for separate general profiles; the
`earn2trade_tcp25` profile blocks order submission, modification, cancellation,
liquidation and copying. Keep `ENABLE_DEFI_AGENTS=false`.

## Repository and development access

[GitHub repository](https://github.com/mohammed-khachachi/alghrest) is private.
Invited collaborators can clone it after accepting access. See
[private collaboration](docs/private-collaboration.md) for setup and the
branch/pull-request workflow. Never commit or share owner credentials.

`main` is the current development tree. Retired reports, recovery dumps and the
older HMM implementation are preserved in the private archive branch
`archive/pre-current-project-cleanup-20261006`, outside `main`. See the
[current file inventory](docs/maintenance/current-project-files.md).

## Repository map

The application uses Python 3.12, asyncio, Pydantic and FastAPI. The general
agent runtime uses Kafka, Redis and PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB; the independent
advisory journal uses SQLite. The dashboard uses React 18, TypeScript and Vite 5.

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/advisory/` | Market/account models, data guards, selection, risk, policies, strategy registry and advice contracts |
| `src/connectors/advisory/` | Replay, durable local research storage and advisory data adapters |
| `src/backtesting/` | Futures fills/costs, edge metrics, path risk, bootstrap, fixed-rule walk-forward and evaluation-event research |
| `src/api/` | Separate advisory API, general API and development mock |
| `src/agents/`, other core/connectors packages | Existing general-profile agents, accounting, messaging and execution/reconciliation |
| `src/ml/` | Experimental model definitions, training and inference service |
| `dashboard/` | React/TypeScript UI with Vite, npm manifest and lockfile |
| `tests/`, `scripts/` | Application tests and developer/operator commands |
| `infra/`, root Compose/Docker files | Schemas, infrastructure definitions, isolated profiles and documented scaffolds |
| `research/hmm_trading/` | Current independent educational HMM study and its own tests/dependencies |
| `artifacts/` | Included model assets and selected synthetic verification records; generated local state is ignored |
| `docs/`, `examples/`, `mcp/` | Guides, standalone Next.js presentation site/static examples and optional model-manager scaffold |

The six Python application packages are installed from `src/`. Import
`core.config`, `api.advisor`, etc.; do not prefix application imports with `src.`.
Research environments and their local `src` package are separate.

## Install the application

Use Python **3.12**. Poetry dependency declarations and `poetry.lock` are the
application dependency source; dashboard dependencies use `npm ci` and the
committed npm lockfile. Docker is needed for service integration work, not for
the local mock/advisory UI.

Windows PowerShell, from the repository root:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/mohammed-khachachi/alghrest.git
Set-Location alghrest
poetry env use 3.12
poetry install
if (-not (Test-Path .env)) { Copy-Item .env.example .env }
```

For every dependency group, use `poetry sync --all-groups`; optional NLP uses
`poetry install --with nlp`. See [quality checks](docs/maintenance/quality-checks.md)
for the full environment and native dependency requirements, and
[lightweight development](docs/LIGHTWEIGHT_DEV.md) for dashboard-only setup.
An existing pip environment with all dependencies installed can install the
application with `python -m pip install --no-deps -e .`.

## Run the advisory assistant

The advisory API listens on **127.0.0.1:8011**. Vite serves the UI on
**127.0.0.1:5173** and proxies `/assistant-api` to it.

Configure a separate local `ADVISORY_ACCESS_TOKEN` before opening the protected
assistant. The access helper, `poetry run python -m scripts.configure_access`,
requires Linux/WSL, preserves existing keys and never prints them. Native Windows
users must follow the local access requirements in
[access setup](docs/maintenance/access-and-ai-limits.md); do not put tokens in
Vite variables, URLs or committed files.

```powershell
$env:OPERATING_PROFILE = "earn2trade_tcp25"
$env:ENABLE_DEFI_AGENTS = "false"
$env:ADVISORY_KAFKA_SERVERS = ""
poetry run python -m api.advisor
# In a second terminal, from the repository root:
Set-Location dashboard
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/assistant` and enter the advisory token locally.
This page uses the independent SQLite research journal and does not open the
trading dashboard WebSocket. See [manual assistant](docs/manual-assistant.md).

Research/domain modules cover MES, MYM, MNQ, MGC, M2K, MCL, M6E, M6B, MHG and NQ.
The manual UI prioritizes NQ/MNQ. Dated contracts, licensed market data and
confirmed account/policy evidence must be supplied explicitly. Missing or
unhealthy inputs remain UNKNOWN/NO TRADE. No broker feed/API entitlement or
account capital is assumed.

## Run the dashboard demo

For ordinary UI development, start the mock backend on loopback port **8000**:

```powershell
poetry run uvicorn api.mock_server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
# In another terminal:
Set-Location dashboard
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/overview`; the mock accepts a blank access key and
supplies demo data. General API and mock share port 8000, so choose one. The
advisory API uses its separate port 8011. See [dashboard README](dashboard/README.md)
for routes, proxies and build commands. Demo quotes/holdings are not actual
licensed market or portfolio evidence.

## Verify changes

Focused application diagnostics, without the full coverage gate:

```powershell
poetry run python scripts/check_architecture.py
poetry run python -m pytest -m unit --no-cov
poetry run ruff check .
```

The default pytest configuration has a **70%** statement/branch coverage gate.
The complete service-backed run uses a disposable local paper/test configuration:

```powershell
# After configuring the isolated endpoints and credentials in the linked guide:
docker compose -f docker-compose.paper.yml up -d --wait --wait-timeout 180
poetry run python -m scripts.paper provision
poetry run python -m scripts.test_with_services -q
```

Follow [quality checks](docs/maintenance/quality-checks.md) and
[isolated execution recovery](docs/execution-recovery.md#isolated-local-infrastructure)
before that command. Do not replace a real account's configuration with test
settings. Provisioning creates schemas/topics, not opening cash balances.

The sanitized local upload snapshot on 2026-10-06 passed **2,112 tests**, with
**53 external-service opt-ins skipped** and **82.16%** combined coverage when
advisory service/backtesting sources were also measured. This is local evidence,
not a hosted CI or live-trading pass. GitHub Actions is configured in
`.github/workflows/tests.yml`; inspect its actual run result. Research tests run
inside their separate HMM directory/environment.

## Research, models and remaining work

Futures research includes explicit fees/slippage, guarded shared strategy rules,
net edge statistics, loss-streak/path analysis, paired block-bootstrap uncertainty,
frozen walk-forward experiments and event-by-event evaluation replay. Synthetic
examples remain EXPERIMENT; they do not certify positive out-of-sample edge or
an official TCP25 pass. Real policy bands, calendar/margin evidence, intraday
extrema coverage, licensed history and calibrated evaluation distributions are
still required. See [migration evidence](docs/maintenance/tcp25-migration.md).

Both existing CNN/PPO assets are included under `artifacts/models/`; the
experimental inference server does not automatically load them. Model presence
is not validation. DeFi and infrastructure scaffolds retain their documented
limitations. Financial opening balances are explicit durable imports;
`SYSTEM_CAPITAL_USD` does not initialize ledger cash.

Start with [documentation](docs/README.md), [architecture](docs/architecture.md),
[development workflow](docs/monorepo-workflow.md), [accounting](docs/accounting.md),
[current HMM research](research/README.md) and [artifact notes](artifacts/README.md).
Read `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and scoped instructions before editing. Keep changes
small, preserve deterministic safety boundaries, add meaningful tests for changed
behavior and submit pull requests for review.

# ALGHREST Dashboard

React 18/TypeScript dashboard and an independent Arabic advisory-assistant page.
The maintained routes are defined in `src/App.tsx`; navigation is in
`src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`. Agent/topic counts depend on backend data;
legacy counts displayed by some demo/UI labels are not an inventory of deployed
services.

## Stack and routes

The package manifest/lockfile define React 18, Vite 5, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI,
React Router, TanStack Query, Zustand, Zod and Recharts.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Redirects to `/overview` |
| `/overview` | Portfolio overview, holdings and market-data panels |
| `/agents` | Agent status and details |
| `/positions` | Position/trade views |
| `/risk` | Risk limits and alerts |
| `/kafka` | Kafka/topic monitoring |
| `/auditor` | Auditor dashboard |
| `/backtest` | Backtest/simulation view |
| `/investor` | Investor presentation |
| `/assistant` | Separate manual research/evaluation assistant |

## Local development

Use Node.js/npm; the Dockerfile uses Node 20. Install from the committed lockfile.
PowerShell, with terminals starting at the repository root:

```powershell
# Terminal 1: loopback-only demo backend on 8000
poetry run uvicorn api.mock_server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
# Terminal 2:
Set-Location dashboard
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/overview`. The mock accepts a blank access key and
returns demo values. Use it for UI work; it does not prove actual account or
market-data health. The general backend also uses 8000, so choose one backend
on that port.

For the protected advisory page, configure its separate local access token and
run `poetry run python -m api.advisor` from the root with
`OPERATING_PROFILE=earn2trade_tcp25`. It binds **8011**. Open
`http://127.0.0.1:5173/assistant`. This page does not connect the trading
WebSocket. See [assistant setup](../docs/manual-assistant.md) and
[local access](../docs/maintenance/access-and-ai-limits.md).

## Connections and access

The Vite dev server binds `127.0.0.1:5173`. Its current proxies are:

| Path | Default target |
| --- | --- |
| `/api` and `/ws` | `http://localhost:8000`, configurable through `VITE_API_URL` |
| `/assistant-api` | `http://127.0.0.1:8011` |
| `/yahoo-api` | Existing Yahoo Finance proxy for the demo UI; not a licensed CME feed |

The WebSocket defaults to the page's same-origin `/ws/dashboard`, using `ws`
or `wss` to match the page protocol. `VITE_WS_URL` can override the full endpoint.
`VITE_API_URL` configures the dev proxy target and is also a Docker build argument;
market-data requests in `src/lib/api.ts` use relative `/api` paths.

Protected general pages use `API_ACCESS_TOKEN`; `/assistant` uses
`ADVISORY_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Tokens are entered in the access gate and retained only
in page memory. Do not put them in Vite variables, browser storage, URLs or Git.
The WebSocket client retries after 3 seconds on disconnect; message channels and
payloads are validated by the schemas in `src/types/ws.ts`. Timing depends on
the connected backend, not a universal update-rate guarantee.

`src/lib/useLiveQuotes.ts` owns shared quote polling every 3 seconds. Subscribe
panels to this hook instead of creating independent `/api/quotes` polling.

## Build and deployment

From `dashboard/`:

```powershell
npm run build
npm run preview
```

`build` runs TypeScript checking then Vite and writes `dist/`. Production hosting
needs SPA routing, correct API/WebSocket reverse proxies and access configuration;
`preview` is a local preview server.

A production image can be built from the dashboard directory:

```powershell
docker build --target production -t alghrest-dashboard .
```

This README's update does not certify an image deployment. Runtime Docker modes
require their documented access/network configuration. See
[root setup](../README.md), [private collaboration](../docs/private-collaboration.md)
and [development workflow](../docs/monorepo-workflow.md) before cross-project work.
The skills under `.agents/skills/` apply only to this dashboard subproject.

# Research

The current independent study is [hmm_trading/](hmm_trading/README.md). It has its
own configuration, references, tests and dependencies. Work inside that directory
with a separate environment; its local Python package named `src` must not be
mixed with the root application import environment.

The HMM pipeline tries Yahoo Finance and falls back to synthetic Markov data on
failure. Label synthetic results explicitly. Its educational in-sample backtest
is not an approved trading strategy or TCP25 pass evidence. Root futures/edge,
bootstrap, walk-forward and evaluation-event tools live in `src/backtesting/`;
[advisory research evidence](../docs/maintenance/tcp25-migration.md) tracks their
limits and validation scope.

The retired `hmm_legacy` study is preserved in the private archive branch
`archive/pre-current-project-cleanup-20261006` and
[immutable snapshot](https://github.com/mohammed-khachachi/alghrest/tree/f88e63be74c2f64ca68c5564c20863f97ca980c8/research/hmm_legacy).
It is outside the current working tree. Keep any root integration explicit and
tested; see [development workflow](../docs/monorepo-workflow.md) and
[integration roadmap](../docs/integration-roadmap.md).

# HMM_Trading

Independent educational Hidden Markov Model study inside ALGHREST. It detects
market regimes, exports charts/results and runs an illustrative backtest. Its
in-sample results do not establish out-of-sample edge or real-trading readiness.
The study does not place broker orders or influence approved root advice.

## Work in the research directory

Use `research/hmm_trading/` with its own environment, dependency file and pytest
configuration. This is part of the private ALGHREST repository, not a separate
Git repository or submodule. Its package is named `src`; do not reuse the root
application environment or run these tests from the repository root.

PowerShell, starting at the ALGHREST root:

```powershell
Set-Location research/hmm_trading
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install pytest
python main.py
python -m pytest tests/
```

The subproject metadata allows Python 3.9+; the main application requires 3.12.
Using a separate 3.12 environment keeps the workspace consistent. The research
requirements use version ranges, not a lockfile; capture installed versions for
reproducible studies. Generate outputs before the artifact test.

## Pipeline and configuration

`main.py` loads `configs/default.json` through `src/core/config.py` and calls
`src/pipeline/runner.py`. The runner locates/extracts reference material, loads
OHLCV data, computes features, fits a Gaussian HMM, decodes/interprets regimes,
builds an educational signal/backtest, and exports metrics and charts.

The data loader attempts Yahoo Finance first. On download/import failure it uses
synthetic Markov-regime data. Check the console's source/fallback messages and
label synthetic outputs explicitly; fallback is not proof of real market access.
The PDF extractor tries pypdf, then PyMuPDF, then its embedded theoretical summary.

See [configuration fields and currently wired controls](configs/README.md).
Schema validation does not mean every configuration field controls pipeline math.
The maintained Stanford PDF is in
`references/Stanford_Hidden_Markov_Models.pdf`; see [reference notes](references/README.md).

## Structure

```text
research/hmm_trading/
  main.py                 Thin command-line entry point
  configs/default.json    Configuration and schema inputs
  src/core/               Configuration, paths and logging
  src/data/               Yahoo loader and synthetic fallback
  src/models/             Features and HMM fitting/decoding
  src/analysis/           Regime interpretation and educational backtest
  src/reporting/          CSV/JSON exports and charts
  src/references/         Reference search and PDF extraction
  tests/                  Unit, integration and generated-output checks
  references/             Included source reference material
  reports/                Research report
  docs/                   Research architecture
  outputs/                Generated locally; ignored by Git
```

## Output and tests

`python main.py` writes result CSVs including `hmm_regimes.csv`,
`state_summary.csv`, `backtest_metrics.csv`, `transition_matrix.csv` and
`backtest_results.csv`, plus `outputs/results/run_config.json`, extracted text and charts.

The artifact test specifically checks these paths:

```text
outputs/results/hmm_regimes.csv
outputs/results/state_summary.csv
outputs/results/backtest_metrics.csv
outputs/results/transition_matrix.csv
outputs/figures/01_price_regimes.png
outputs/figures/02_equity_curves.png
outputs/figures/03_regime_distribution.png
outputs/figures/04_transition_matrix.png
```

From this directory, use `python -m pytest tests/` for all tests, or target
`tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/`, or `tests/artifacts/`. Missing generated
outputs cause the artifact test to fail with an instruction to run `main.py`.
Generated output files, `.venv` and caches are not committed.

## Development and root integration

Read `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and [research architecture](docs/architecture.md)
before changes. Preserve outputs/reports/references, keep mathematical changes
explicit, and follow scoped pipeline/test verification. Root integration remains
a separate task requiring an explicit CSV/CLI/API contract and tests; the study
is not automatically wired into ALGHREST production decisions.

See the root [research index](../README.md),
[development workflow](../../docs/monorepo-workflow.md),
[integration roadmap](../../docs/integration-roadmap.md) and
[private collaborator setup](../../docs/private-collaboration.md).

# Model assets and research evidence

This directory separates included development assets from generated local state.
It is excluded from the runtime wheel and Docker application build context.

## Included in the private repository

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `models/cnn_btc_usdt.pth` | Existing CNN checkpoint |
| `models/ppo_position_sizer.zip` | Existing PPO archive |
| `tcp25-goal/` | Selected synthetic examples and verification summaries for advisory, risk, replay and research work |

Training code writes CNN/PPO files to `models/`. The current experimental
inference server creates a CNN in memory and does not automatically load these
assets; its RL action is still a placeholder. Existing file bytes are preserved,
but their presence does not establish training provenance, predictive edge or
production readiness. Only load trusted serialized model files.

The before-code snapshot under `tcp25-goal/trade-management/before/` is a fixture
for an explicit opt-in regression comparison, not a second runtime agent.
Synthetic evaluation PASS examples are conditional calculations, not proof of a
completed official evaluation. Saved research results are pinned to code/input
fingerprints and must be verified with the matching implementation.

## Generated local files

`.gitignore` excludes other generated models, checkpoints, test reports, datasets,
logs and SQLite/account state. `artifacts/advisory/research.sqlite3` is the local
research journal; use SQLite backup for an active journal, never commit it.
The two model assets and selected evidence were intentionally tracked despite
broader generated-file ignore rules.

Keep important model versions and evaluation provenance in durable backed-up
storage before cleanup. Do not publish secrets, private licensed data, financial
stores or raw operational logs. See [current project files](../docs/maintenance/current-project-files.md)
and [private development](../docs/private-collaboration.md).

## Evidence and limits

Dated test/verification sections describe their original code and environment.
Local passing tests do not certify hosted CI, complete TCP25 evaluation, a live
feed or real-account readiness. Synthetic strategy/evaluation records remain
experiments. Current source and selected verification records stay in `main`;
real credentials, financial stores, licensed/private datasets and raw operational
logs are not shared through Git.

Retired reports, raw recovery outputs, old paper-readiness data and the older HMM
implementation remain in the private archive branch
`archive/pre-current-project-cleanup-20261006` and
[its immutable snapshot](https://github.com/mohammed-khachachi/alghrest/tree/f88e63be74c2f64ca68c5564c20863f97ca980c8).
Their original paths and results are historical evidence, not current setup inputs.
